combat_tables.description: Attack resolution tables for the Lord of the Rings Galaxy tabletop game. Adapted from Legion (ground), X-Wing (space), and Rebellion (galaxy-scale) mechanics.

ground_combat.description: Ground combat uses red (attack) and yellow (defense) dice. Results are modified by range, cover, and unit abilities.

attack_dice_results.hit: Deals 1 damage to the target. Applied to shields first, then hull.
attack_dice_results.glance: Deals 1 damage, but can be blocked by certain abilities. Less reliable than a hit.
attack_dice_results.crit: Deals 1 damage and triggers a critical effect (e.g., suppression, disruption, or extra damage).

defense_dice_results.evade: Removes 1 Hit or Glance from the attack.
defense_dice_results.shield: Removes 1 Hit or Glance. Some units have limited shield tokens.

range_modifiers.range_1: Close range — full attack dice, no penalty
range_modifiers.range_2: Medium range — full attack dice, no penalty (most weapons)
range_modifiers.range_3: Long range — may reduce attack dice or add penalties

cover_modifiers.heavy_cover: +2 yellow defense dice; may block line of sight

damage_resolution.shields_first: Damage is applied to shield wounds first. Shield wounds heal during the end phase.
damage_resolution.hull_second: Once shields are depleted, damage is applied to hull wounds. Hull wounds are permanent until the unit is removed.
damage_resolution.unit_eliminated: When a unit's hull wounds reach its wound threshold, it is eliminated.

special_effects.suppression: Unit cannot shoot until it recovers. Recovers at the end of the owner's next activation.
special_effects.disruption: Unit cannot activate next round. Affects command and strategy.
special_effects.fear: Unit flees if it takes a critical hit. Cannot return until the fear source is removed.
special_effects.hope: Free Peoples units near a Hope source gain +1 defense dice.

space_combat.description: Space combat uses red (attack) and green (defense) dice. Critical hits impose lasting damage cards.

attack_dice_results.hit: Deals 1 damage. Assign a face-down damage card to the defending ship.
attack_dice_results.crit: Deals 1 damage and reveals the damage card face-up (critical hit with ongoing effect).
attack_dice_results.focus: Can be converted to a Hit, or used to add 1 green defense dice to a friendly ship.

defense_dice_results.evade: Removes 1 Hit or Crit from the attack.
defense_dice_results.shield: If the ship has shields, removes 1 Hit or Crit and does not assign a damage card (shield absorbs it).

damage_cards.stress: Ship cannot perform actions next activation (most common face-down result)
damage_cards.hit: No ongoing effect — just damage absorption (face-down)
critical_hits: Hull Breach — ship takes extra damage
Shield Modulator Failure — shields cannot regenerate
Weapon Malfunction — ship loses attack dice

firing_arc_rules.front_arc: Most ships can only attack in their front 120-degree arc
firing_arc_rules.full_arc: Some ships (e.g., Elven Ships, Barad-dûr) can attack in any direction
firing_arc_rules.overlap: Ships cannot overlap at the end of a maneuver; if they do, the later ship is pushed back

galaxy_scale_combat.description: Galaxy-scale combat uses standard six-sided dice (d6) with tactic card modifiers.

space_combat.description: Ship-to-ship combat in a star system. Uses attack values from ships and tactic card modifiers.
steps: Attacker declares space combat in a system
Both players draw or play a space tactic card
Each player rolls d6s equal to their total ship attack values
Hits are assigned to opposing ships' shields first, then hull
tactic_card_effects: Prevent opponent from rolling certain values
One in a Million: auto-hit (special card — e.g., Elven archers never miss)

ground_combat.description: Ground combat to determine system loyalty. Winner gains loyalty markers.
steps: Attacker declares ground combat in a system
Both players draw or play a ground tactic card
Each player rolls d6s equal to their total ground unit attack values
Player with more hits gains loyalty in the system

loyalty_system.description: Systems have loyalty to either the Free Peoples or the Forces of Darkness. Loyalty is gained through ground combat and mission completion.
loyalty_system.free_peoples_system: System with Free Peoples loyalty marker — Free Peoples gain benefits when operating there
loyalty_system.dark_system: System with Forces of Darkness loyalty marker — Forces of Darkness gain benefits when operating there
loyalty_system.neutral_system: System with no loyalty marker — no faction benefits
loyalty_system.contested_system: System with both loyalty markers — combat bonuses for both sides

ring_bearer_combat.description: Special combat rules for encounters involving the Ring-bearer.

ring_bearer_encounters.description: When the Ring-bearer is discovered by enemy forces, a special combat encounter occurs.
steps: The Ring-bearer's corruption increases by 1 stage
Companion units (e.g., Sam, Gollum) can intervene
The Ring-bearer can use the Phial of Galadriel or Sting for defense
If the Ring-bearer is captured, the Forces of Darkness win
If the Ring-bearer escapes, the corruption increases but the quest continues

gollum_mechanic.description: Gollum is a wildcard unit that can switch sides based on the split personality mechanic.
mechanics: Gollum can betray either side at any time
The player controlling Gollum can choose which personality acts
At Mount Doom, Gollum's obsession determines the outcome

narrative_dice.description: For RPG-style encounters, narrative dice pools are used with success/failure, advantage/threat, and triumph/despair.

dice_types.ability: Represents the character's skill. Rolls for Success and Advantage.
dice_types.boost: Added by favorable circumstances. Rolls for extra Success.
dice_types.advantage: Added by favorable positioning. Rolls for extra Advantage.
dice_types.difficulty: Set by the GM. Rolls for Failure and Threat.
dice_types.challenge: Added by complications. Rolls for extra Failure.
dice_types.despair: Rare; added by extreme danger. Rolls for automatic Despair.

results.success: The action succeeds. Each Success over Failure determines the degree.
results.failure: The action fails. Each Failure over Success determines the degree.
results.advantage: Side benefit — extra information, positioning, or resources.
results.threat: Side cost — danger, complications, or resource loss.
results.triumph: Major success — always counts as Success and triggers a major positive narrative effect.
results.despair: Major failure — always counts as Failure and triggers a major negative narrative effect.
